stemMd: An opaque unit cube occupies $0\leq x,y,z\leq1$. An observer is at $(2,2,2)$ looking toward its centre. Which three outer faces can be visible simultaneously?
explanationMd: The viewer lies on the positive side of each coordinate direction. The outward-facing surfaces nearest that octant are the three faces with coordinate one. Each opposite face is hidden by the convex solid.

distractorRationale.c: These face away from the viewer in the stated octant.
distractorRationale.b: Opposite parallel faces cannot both be directly visible on an opaque convex cube.
distractorRationale.e: This includes opposite faces of the opaque cube.
distractorRationale.a: An exterior view cannot see through the opaque cube.
